record.context_brief: Algorithmic complexity of graph diameter computation.
record.original_question: Find a faster algorithm for computing the diameter of a graph than the matrix-multiplication-based bound cited in the source.

evidence.quote: Find a fast algorithm to determine the diameter of a graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph on $n=|V|$ vertices and $m=|E|$ edges. The distance $d_G(u,v)$ between two vertices $u,v\in V$ is the number of edges in a shortest path from $u$ to $v$ (or $+\infty$ if no such path exists). The diameter of $G$ is
$$\mathrm{diam}(G) \;=\; \max_{u,v\in V} d_G(u,v).$$

It is known that $\mathrm{diam}(G)$ can be computed by first solving all-pairs shortest paths, which via fast (Boolean/min-plus) matrix multiplication can be done in time $O(n^{\omega})$ for unweighted graphs, where $\omega<2.373$ is the matrix-multiplication exponent.

Problem. Design an algorithm that computes the exact diameter $\mathrm{diam}(G)$ of an arbitrary (say unweighted, undirected) graph $G$ in time asymptotically faster than the matrix-multiplication-based $O(n^{\omega})$ bound; equivalently, determine whether exact diameter computation is strictly easier than all-pairs shortest paths, or prove that no such speed-up is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact complexity of computing graph diameter remains open. The fastest exact algorithm still runs in $O(n^{\omega})$ time via fast matrix multiplication, and it is a well-known open question whether exact diameter requires solving all-pairs shortest paths. Conditional lower bounds under SETH rule out truly subquadratic $O((n+m)^{2-\varepsilon})$ algorithms for sparse graphs, but no unconditional improvement over the matrix-multiplication bound is known, and approximation/directed/dynamic variants remain active research areas.

status_evidence.title: CS 267 Lecture 3 Shortest paths, graph diameter (Vassilevska Williams)
status_evidence.snippet: The (theoretically) fastest algorithm for Diameter runs in O(n^{2.373}) time and is based on fast matrix multiplication.
status_evidence.claim: Best known exact diameter algorithm is the matrix-multiplication-based O(n^ω) bound.

status_evidence.title: Fast Approximation Algorithms for the Diameter and Radius of Sparse Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Solving Diameter in O((n+m)^{2-ε}) time for any ε > 0 breaks the SETH.
status_evidence.claim: Truly subquadratic exact diameter algorithms in sparse graphs would refute SETH, leaving the question of improving the matrix-multiplication bound open.

status_evidence.title: On Diameter Approximation in Directed Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: It remains a big open problem whether computing the diameter of a graph exactly requires computing APSP.
status_evidence.claim: Whether exact diameter is easier than APSP is explicitly stated as an open problem in 2023.
